Andersons - Quality For The Home Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Caturra Lights
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse trained by Adrian Keatley, absent 102 days which is a significant fitness query, but the form figures of 3-3-9 show consistent minor placings at up to 6f on Good ground; if sharper than the layoff suggests, she could be a late threat at a big price.

runners_data.name: Fast Performer
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (just two runs) and trained by the in-form William Haggas (T14: 13/48), which is an eye-catching angle; Cieren Fallon in the saddle is a further plus, and a hood is fitted for the first time — caught wide at Newmarket last time suggests this step to Carlisle could suit if she settles better.

runners_data.name: North Star Kodi
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for the powerful Fahey yard, absent 105 days which is a notable concern given the absence of any prep run; both starts have been on Good ground at 5-6f, so going and trip pose no obvious issues, but peak fitness must be assumed on trust.

runners_data.name: Social Spirit
runners_data.note: Lightly exposed but holds a sim-going run (1st of 6 on similar conditions) which stands out in this field; Billy Garritty keeps the ride, the Easterby yard is ticking along at 4/33 in the last fortnight, and the recent form string shows gradual improvement — the Going record here is the most compelling factor.

runners_data.name: Donegal Rose
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter whose OR=69 win at 6f on Good ground last time out underpins her claims; Hugo Palmer has only 2/30 in 14 days but the horse's ability to dictate from the front on a flat 6f track is the key tactical asset, though a style-fit flag (0.92) reminds us she can be caught when the pace collapses late.

runners_data.name: My Normandie
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature, pushed into a midfield slot on the map because the field is saturated with closers; George Scott's 2/16 in 14 days is modest, form figures of 7-5-6-5 are uninspiring, and the 62-day absence adds another layer of doubt over her chance in a race where her true style is unlikely to be rewarded.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Gift
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners this Kevin Ryan runner whose three starts have all been on Good or Soft-similar ground (0W0P on soft-sim); mapped to midfield but a true hold-up type unlikely to get her natural position — the 0.90 style-fit flag is the lowest in the field, and the form sequence of 7-5-3 at 6-7f suggests she needs things to fall just right.

runners_data.name: State Of Gold
runners_data.note: The most interesting of the redistributed closers — won over 8f last time and finished second over this 6f trip, suggesting she stays well and could be underestimated on a flat course; Craig Lidster's yard is quiet (1/7 in 14 days) but recent form of 8-5-7-2-1 shows she is in good nick, and the step back to 6f is the only real question.

runners_data.name: Ponte Carlo
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner with headgear (p) applied and 2/6 sim-going placed runs to his name, which shows he handles conditions; a true hold-up type displaced to midfield on the map, and with a 5lb claimer (Jake Dickson) up, the combination of slow pace and inexperienced rider makes a winning challenge genuinely difficult.

runners_data.name: Excessive
runners_data.note: Another Tim Easterby hold-up horse mapped to midfield by necessity rather than natural preference; headgear worn (p), 1/4 on similar going (placed), and a 29-day turnaround suggests she is fit, but OR=60 makes her the lowest-rated runner in the field and the modest rating reflects the modest form figures throughout.

races.paceDynamic: Donegal Rose is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 2yo nursery handicap over 6f on Good to Soft ground at Carlisle, and with no genuine pace rivals to push her, she is able to dictate terms at whatever tempo she chooses — creating a controlled, single-pace affair rather than a truly searching test. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types: State Of Gold, My Normandie, Harlequin Gift, Ponte Carlo, and Excessive are all natural hold-up runners who have been redistributed into midfield slots on the map simply because there are too many true closers to accommodate at the rear. On Good to Soft ground over 6f at Carlisle — a flat, galloping track where the straight run-in rewards those who travel well through a race — a moderate, uncontested gallop set by Donegal Rose is likely to compress the field, making it difficult for genuine hold-up horses to find daylight and generate meaningful momentum in the closing stages. The race shape most clearly favours prominent racers or those able to sit close to the pace and quicken from a position of travelling comfort, with deep closers carrying extra risk given the likely lack of a truly strong early pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Donegal Rose Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Donegal Rose leads without serious early pressure and sets a measured tempo that denies the closers a true target.
scenarios.body: Donegal Rose controls proceedings from the front on her own terms, the pack bunches behind her, and those positioned prominently — or moving smoothly into contention — get first run entering the final two furlongs; closers simply cannot generate enough momentum against a modest gallop on a flat track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Storm Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the ground rides slower than Good to Soft, creating a proper test that sets up a late surge.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated tempo from Donegal Rose — perhaps hustled by early movers — burns off the leaders, leaving the field strung out and creating genuine gaps for late runners to exploit; the softer the ground rides in reality, the more stamina becomes the deciding factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Donegal Rose sets a crawl and the race explodes in the final furlong with a mass sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A very slow early pace bunches the entire field together approaching the two-furlong pole, turning the race into a flat-out dash where position at the furlong pole is everything; horses with a sharp turn of foot from mid-division are best placed, but the outcome is chaotic and form-lines count for little.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Donegal Rose is caught out by the ground in the final furlong and a close-tracking rival swoops past her.
scenarios.body: Donegal Rose's stamina is found wanting in the final 100 yards on the testing surface, and whichever runner has tracked her closely in second or third position — travelling within herself — hits the front and holds on; this outcome requires Donegal Rose to stop, which her profile makes less than likely.

watchPoints.text: Donegal Rose's early splits will define this race — watch whether she is allowed to idle in front or whether the pace is faster than it appears, as this determines whether closers can get competitive.

Fast Performer is first-time headgear and lightly raced — Cieren Fallon will look to get her travelling smoothly off the pace, and if she relaxes early she could outrun her current odds on the Haggas angle alone.

State Of Gold has won over 8f and her hold-up style is a mismatch for a potentially slow 6f pace — watch whether Clifford Lee opts to push her forward early against her natural grain, as that tactical decision could either unlock or ruin her chance.

The Good to Soft going report is consistent across all seven races at Carlisle today — ground is genuine and unlikely to ride significantly faster or slower than described, which tempers any going-related variance.

Social Spirit's sim-going form (1st of 6 on similar conditions) is the standout piece of ground-relevant evidence in the field — worth monitoring her in the market as a potential value angle if conditions are cited as a positive by connections.

races.name: Lpd Maiden Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Lord Byron
runners_data.note: Veteran of stayers' handicap company dropping into maiden class; solid sim-going record (7/8), Faye Bramley's sole front-runner here, and 131 days off the track could mean he arrives fresh — style fit slightly inflated at 0.92 since his natural P tag is an underplay of how leadingly he is likely to race in this shape.

runners_data.name: Togeather Forever
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old has only two runs in the book, both on soft or good-to-soft, but finished fifth and sixth from a hold-up berth; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a bonus, though the horse needs a stronger pace than this race may provide.

runners_data.name: Act Of Generosity
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-year-old placed twice on good ground over 10f; stepping up markedly to 1m3f and encountering soft going for the first time are the key questions, though Varian regularly targets trips like this as a confidence builder for progressing types.

runners_data.name: Blue Hercules
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with five seconds in his form string, Daniel Tudhope takes the ride; however, his true racing style is at the back of the field — appearing in midfield on this map only because genuine hold-up horses outnumber available rear positions, so his real closing run will be launched from further back than his map slot implies.

runners_data.name: Casement Park
runners_data.note: Simon West debutant with zero form data; going and style entirely unknown, and with a trainer who had just one runner in the past 14 days, there is little to build a case on — monitor market moves for any stable intelligence.

runners_data.name: Chico Dorado
runners_data.note: First-time-out runner for Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore, with Oisin Orr a booking that commands attention on debut; an entirely unknown quantity on soft ground and at 1m3f, so watch whether he moves fluently through the conditions early.

runners_data.name: Flagbearer
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends James Doyle north for this, which is a significant booking; third on soft ground at 11f last time gives him a genuine profile for these conditions, though his hold-up style leaves him at the mercy of the pace Lord Byron sets.

runners_data.name: Impierious
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's horse has been remarkably consistent with four consecutive thirds, all on good ground at shorter distances; steps up to 1m3f on soft today for the first time, but his prominent style is ideal if he can track Lord Byron and quicken off a manageable gallop — headgear note: visor worn.

runners_data.name: Mighty Wave
runners_data.note: Daragh Bourke's three-year-old holds some form on soft ground (3/4 sim-going) and placed at 12f on his second start; like Blue Hercules, his genuine tactical preference is to race from off the pace, placed into midfield here only because the hold-up cluster is too large for the map — David Nolan will need a proper pace to use him to effect.

runners_data.name: Wadacre Icon
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston has a strong record from a limited sample (2/32 in 14 days) and Connor Beasley is a reliable northern jockey; completely unexposed on debut, which is both the risk and the appeal in a race where class levels are moderate.

runners_data.name: Harper Violet
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's filly has 151 days between runs, which is notable, and her form includes a third on soft ground at 7f; the step to 1m3f is significant, but Burke is adept at placing horses fresh after a break, and Clifford Lee is a competent ally if she handles the trip.

runners_data.name: Lazy In Red
runners_data.note: Donald Whillans sends out a horse with just one run — a third on soft ground at 11f — which is the only benchmark; the trip suits and the going is no concern, but from a hold-up berth she needs something to chase that Lord Byron may not provide.

races.paceDynamic: Lord Byron is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-horse field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival likely to press him hard from the outset on Good to Soft ground over 1m3f at Carlisle. With Impierious as the only other naturally prominent type, Lord Byron can control tempo from the front, dictating a steady-to-moderate gallop that plays directly into his hands — and with 131 days off the track, his freshness on a surface he handles (7/8 on sim-going) is a live factor. The hold-up brigade — Flagbearer, Harper Violet, Lazy In Red, Togeather Forever — will need a strong enough pace to bring them into play off the turn, and with only one true pace-setter, that is not guaranteed. Blue Hercules and Mighty Wave are genuine hold-up types who have been mapped into midfield purely because the rear of the field is congested; neither will naturally get a prominent berth, meaning their redistribution is cosmetic and should not disguise their true closer profile. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can travel just off the pace and pounce when Lord Byron inevitably ties up, rather than deep hold-up horses relying on a strong pace that may never materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lord Byron Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lord Byron breaks cleanly and sets a comfortable solo lead, dictating a moderate tempo that starves the closers of a true pace.
scenarios.body: Lord Byron settles into a rhythm from the front on ground he handles well, and with Impierious as the only shadowing presence, he controls the race end to end; the soft ground at 1m3f tests stamina rather than speed, suiting a horse that can conserve energy in front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lord Byron is tracked closely by Impierious or Act Of Generosity, who time their run to nail him approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A moderate pace set by Lord Byron leaves the prominent runners in a perfect stalking position with energy to spare, and when Lord Byron flattens out on the soft ground, the horse travelling most smoothly off his back has first run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the field strings out, giving hold-up horses a meaningful target to reel in.
scenarios.body: Flagbearer or Harper Violet, both proven on soft ground and handled by quality jockeys in James Doyle and Clifford Lee, could benefit if Lord Byron goes a fraction too quick and burns off Impierious, creating a collapsing front and a late rush.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexposed Type Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three lightly-raced unknowns — Casement Park, Chico Dorado or Wadacre Icon — proves significantly better than their debut form suggests.
scenarios.body: An unexposed maiden with natural stamina for 1m3f on soft ground can emerge from anywhere in the field if the management of pace exposes ordinary rivals; Charlie Johnston's Wadacre Icon or Oisin Orr on Chico Dorado are the most interesting unknown quantities.

watchPoints.text: Lord Byron's early break and settling pattern are critical — if he jumps cleanly and is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, the race shape locks in immediately and prominent trackers must react within the first furlong.

Blue Hercules and Mighty Wave are both mapped into midfield but will race from hold-up positions in practice; watch whether David Nolan and Daniel Tudhope find themselves trapped on the rail with nowhere to go if the field compresses behind Lord Byron's slow pace.

Impierious wears a visor and has been third in all four starts — the headgear context combined with the first-time test at 1m3f on soft ground makes his sectionals in the middle part of the race the key indicator of whether he can finally convert.

The three debutants — Casement Park, Chico Dorado and Wadacre Icon — should be tracked in the betting ring before post time; any significant market move, particularly for Wadacre Icon given Charlie Johnston's shrewdness, would elevate their relevance considerably.

Flagbearer's booking of James Doyle for a Haggas hold-up horse in a race likely to be run at a moderate pace is worth monitoring — if Doyle elects to sit much closer than Flagbearer's natural style suggests, it signals the yard expects the horse to be competitive regardless of shape.

races.name: Deanta Fire Door Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Cape Sovereign
runners_data.note: Gelded hold-up operator returning from a lengthy 328-day absence for Rebecca Menzies, who has only one winner from 17 runs in the last fortnight; the long layoff is the dominant concern and soft ground is unfamiliar territory based on his recent form string.|

runners_data.name: Cotai Starlight
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine pace-setter; Katie Scott's three-year-old comes here off a 13-day turnaround, has winning form over 5f on good ground, and her natural front-running role gives her a structural advantage in a field that cannot pressure her early — though the STYLE_FIT tag notes she is technically flagged as racing slightly out of optimum role.|

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's eight-year-old veteran carries prominent-style headgear (p) and has a win at 5f on good in recent outings; similar-going returns (1W from 15 runs) are modest but this experienced sprinter knows how to get competitive late and Jake Dickson's 5lb claim is a meaningful weight relief.|

runners_data.name: Bibendum
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who carries headgear (p) and won over 5f on good ground earlier in the season for Julie Camacho; form has gone backwards since that win, and soft ground brings an unknown element given all recent efforts have been on good or quicker.|

runners_data.name: Go Victor
runners_data.note: Tony Culhane's three-year-old has soft-ground and all-weather form in his last five runs, suggesting he handles conditions, but his best effort came over 6f and the drop to 5f flat is a query — his trainer has zero winners from three runs in the past fortnight.|

runners_data.name: Midnight Lir
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, wearing headgear (tv), but the congested field forces him forward from his natural position; similar-going record (0W0P from 15) is a significant concern on this surface, and Connor Beasley will need gaps that may not appear.|

runners_data.name: Solid Bond
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's four-year-old arrives fresh from an 83-day break, wears headgear (t), and has soft-ground experience in his form string (3/5f/STA, 7/5f/SOF) giving him a genuine claim on the conditions; his prominent racing style is a tactical asset in this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Brian Rothwell's six-year-old is a true closer whose natural station is at the rear, but the crowded hold-up section means he cannot drop in fully; headgear (tp) suggests he needs motivation, and a 0W record in similar going from 15 runs is a hard fact to ignore.|

runners_data.name: Never Dark
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's veteran sprinter has placed in similar going (0W1P from 15) and his recent form includes a second at 5f on good; he will be squeezed forward from his natural hold-up berth — his 9yo legs have won at 5f before but the race shape here is not set up to flatter late-runners.|

runners_data.name: Pivotal Terms
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Iain Jardine ridden by 7lb claimer Cara Tuke; ran only seven days ago which is a quick turnaround, soft-ground record is unproven (2 of 15 exposed runs), and as a natural hold-up type forced into midfield the combination of inexperience and traffic risk is notable.|

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's five-year-old has won at 5f on good (1/5f/GOO in last five) and wears headgear (tp), but his similar-going record (0W0P from 15) is a red flag; naturally a hold-up horse who will be operating ahead of his comfort zone tactically in this scenario.|

runners_data.name: Kyber Crystal
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' seven-year-old is a genuine prominent racer (style=P) who has won in similar going (1W2P from 15 soft-ground runs) — the most encouraging soft-ground strike rate among the prominent types; wears headgear (tp) and Cieren Fallon is a strong booking from stall draw.|

runners_data.name: Bust A Moon
runners_data.note: Derek Shaw's four-year-old runs off the back of a six-day turnaround and wears headgear (h), indicating he can be tricky to settle; his 5f form on easy ground includes a third at Sandown (3/5f/STA) and he has placed on soft ground before, giving him marginal conditions credentials among the true hold-up brigade.|

races.paceDynamic: Cotai Starlight is the one confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner sprint, and on soft ground over 5f at Carlisle she is likely to stride into a clear early lead with Sam James allowing her to find her own rhythm unchallenged. With no other genuine leader in the field, the pace will be set by a single horse rather than a contested battle, creating a sustainable gallop that keeps the race honest but never becomes a true burn-up — a classic scenario on soft ground where the leader can control fractions. The field behind will bunch through the middle stages as the redistributed hold-up horses (Midnight Lir, Opal Storm, Never Dark, Pivotal Terms, Royal Duke, Bust A Moon) are shuffled into midfield positions that are not their natural home, creating congestion and making it harder for true closers to find the daylight they need. This race shape — a solo leader controlling pace on a softening surface — most strongly favours prominent racers who can track Cotai Starlight at close quarters and pounce in the final furlong, giving the edge to those with the tactical positioning to challenge at the two-pole mark rather than those relying on a late run through a compressed field. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear, with Midnight Lir, Opal Storm, and Never Dark among the most likely to push forward and contest prominent positions ahead of their natural finishing style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates On Soft
scenarios.trigger: If Cotai Starlight leads unchallenged and the soft ground rewards controlled front-running.
scenarios.body: Cotai Starlight bowls along at her own tempo on a surface that suits her recent winning form, and the absence of pressure means she can conserve energy for the final furlong push; horses who track her in second and third are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If horses tracking prominently close Cotai Starlight down in the final 100 yards as the soft ground takes its toll.
scenarios.body: The leader's energy is sapped by the testing ground in the closing stages, and any horse sitting two to three lengths off the pace with cover has the momentum to reel her in; a prominent racer with soft-ground form benefits most here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Weave Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to unwind the field and allow hold-up horses a clear passage to the stands rail.
scenarios.body: The bunched midfield separates in the final two furlongs, giving a genuine closer room to pick off tiring rivals; however, this requires both a hot early gallop and clear daylight, which is harder to engineer when so many hold-up horses are not in their natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the going deteriorates significantly and the race dissolves into a stamina-test where form lines are meaningless.
scenarios.body: Slower conditions punish those without soft-ground credentials while elevating horses carrying less weight with proven stamina reserves; the handicap is reshuffled by the surface rather than the pace shape.

watchPoints.text: Cotai Starlight's front-running role gives her full control of fractions — if Sam James allows her to bowl along unchallenged, she could prove very hard to reel in on softening ground and the field should be watched for whether anyone contests her early.|

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Midnight Lir, Opal Storm, Never Dark, Royal Duke, Pivotal Terms, Bust A Moon) will create significant midfield congestion — watch for interference and horses failing to get a clear run in the straight as a consequence of unnatural positioning.|

Solid Bond returns from an 83-day break as a prominent racer with soft-ground form — horses returning fresh with established soft-ground profiles can outrun their odds first time back, and Zak Wheatley should have him handy from the outset.|

Kyber Crystal is the only prominent-style runner (aside from Cotai Starlight) with a recorded win on similar going — watch where she slots in behind the leader, as her position in the first two furlongs will dictate whether she can mount a serious challenge.|

The going report for this exact race slot (3:47 5f) is listed as Good To Soft rather than Soft — if the actual surface is on the quicker end of that range, Cotai Starlight's form on good ground becomes more relevant and the advantage swings further toward the prominent types.|

races.name: Quickstep Supporting Andersons Autumn Flooring Offers Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Velvet Skies
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with visor fitted and a creditable soft-ground run (2nd of 15 at similar going) in her recent history; 8 days since last run is fine, but she needs cover and a strong pace to close into — the controlled tempo Bay Breeze is likely to set is her key concern.

runners_data.name: Donald
runners_data.note: Returned a solid 2nd at Carlisle on Soft in his most recent winning-quality run and handles this track; Callum Rodriguez takes the ride for a trainer who is cold at 0/11 in the last 14 days, and his prominent form figures at this course give him a shout if the race develops with any tempo.

runners_data.name: Bay Breeze
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and key pace-setter; Tim Easterby is in fine form (14/81 in 14 days) and this 7-year-old has multiple Soft-going runs on his card, including a third at 6f on Soft — uncontested lead on Good to Soft at Carlisle sets him up as a live player, not just a pacemaker.

runners_data.name: Run This Way
runners_data.note: Prominent-style racer who has won twice at 6f on Good ground and placed three times in five recent runs; blinkers fitted and David Nolan in the saddle is a strong positive, though he has found soft ground less productive in his history and the going is the one reservation against a horse otherwise ideally positioned in the race shape.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from the Tim Easterby yard (same in-form handler as Bay Breeze) wearing a visor; his recent form at 6f on Good ground has shown top-three placings but his last two runs at 7f on Stanwick were poor — dropping back to 6f and tracking a stablemate could see a bounce back, though soft ground is a mild query.

runners_data.name: Zous Juice
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has shown his best form at 7f-8f and finds 6f a minimum; his one similar-going run produced a second at 7f/Soft which is encouraging, but Billy Garritty is riding a horse that may find this trip on the short side at this distance with a pedestrian pace to close off.

runners_data.name: Little Beck Annie
runners_data.note: Showed a win at 6f on Good and has consistent placed form at sprint trips; despite being a natural hold-up horse, the crowded rear means she is likely to race off her true position — her Soft-going profile is unknown from her recent hist, and that style displacement tempers confidence despite Daniel Tudhope's presence.

runners_data.name: Wee Dresser
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old who has been running consistently in the 3rd-8th range at 6f on Good; her true style is as a hold-up racer but the field's composition forces her forward, an uncomfortable shift — 58 days off the track is the longest layoff in this field and freshness could cut either way on soft going.

runners_data.name: Dream Forever
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Soft and placed on Soft, making her the hold-up runner with the strongest case for soft-ground form in this field; however, the redistribution to midfield means she is unlikely to secure the position her style demands — Jack Nicholls (3lb claimer) rides, and only 6 days since her last run suggests she is race-fit.

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose best recent run was a 2nd at 6f on Good and a 3rd at 5f; Lauren Young's 5lb claim helps at the weights but the horse has no soft-going form in the recent record and the enforced positional compromise makes finding her best very difficult in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Runninman
runners_data.note: The 3-year-old from Donald Whillans has been running at 6f-7f on Good and Soft without threatening, with a low-water-mark of 12th at 6f on Stanwick; tongue-tie added, Greg Fairley rides — a genuine back-marker by inclination who must race closer than he wants here, and with the least convincing form figures in the field, his chance is marginal.

races.paceDynamic: Bay Breeze is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, Duran Fentiman should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, energy-efficient tempo on this Good to Soft Carlisle turf. Run This Way and Fan Mail will push forward to challenge for prominent positions just behind, creating a race that unfolds at a steady-to-moderate gallop rather than a breakneck sprint — conditions that suit a horse able to travel close to the pace and quicken on a surface that tends to favour those with cover from the early exchanges. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Little Beck Annie, Wee Dresser, Dream Forever, Summerstorms Dream and Runninman are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, meaning the positions they need in a true closer's race are unlikely to materialise in this shape. With one unchallenged pace-setter controlling from the front and soft ground blunting finishing speed, the race strongly favours horses who can track the leader in second or third gear — prominent racers who get a clean tow into the race — rather than those relying on a strong late run off a searching pace that simply will not be set.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bay Breeze Controls, Proximity Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Bay Breeze is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a comfortable tempo that rewards those tracking close.
scenarios.body: Bay Breeze gets a soft lead on Good to Soft ground and those settled just off the pace in second and third position get the ideal tow into the race without burning early energy; the controlled gallop means closers have no deep pace to attack off, and race shape rewards those with positional speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Them Down
scenarios.trigger: If Run This Way and Fan Mail both press Bay Breeze harder than expected and the trio set a stronger pace that suits grinders over closers.
scenarios.body: The early pace lifts slightly as multiple prominent horses compete for position, softening the leaders but still not creating the strong-enough gallop for pure hold-up horses to come from last; a horse with stamina and positional coverage can pick off tiring rivals in the final furlong on this soft ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and allow a repositioned hold-up type to close powerfully.
scenarios.body: Dream Forever and Zous Juice — both who showed soft-ground form in their histories — would be the most likely beneficiaries if an unexpectedly strong gallop creates the conditions for a late run, though this shape is discounted because the true hold-up types have been redistributed and are unlikely to secure the rearward position they need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the ground rides slower than the official Good to Soft description and produces a stop-start, attritional finish where stamina and freshness dominate.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses fail to handle the testing underfoot conditions and the race degenerates into a stamina test where the freshest, most resolute stayer grinds past tiring rivals close home; runners returning quickly off short breaks with soft-ground form scores most here.

watchPoints.text: Bay Breeze — watch whether Fentiman is truly allowed a soft lead from the gates; if he establishes an uncontested front-running position inside the first furlong, he becomes the dominant tactical force in this race and the entire shape locks in around him.

Run This Way — observe the early stride out of the stalls; if he or Fan Mail immediately pushes forward to challenge Bay Breeze rather than settling, the pace lifts and the scenario shifts from controlled to genuinely contested, changing which profiles benefit.

Dream Forever — despite being redistributed to midfield on the map, watch if Jack Nicholls drops her out sharply at the start to find her natural hold-up berth; if she achieves true back-marker position she is the most likely disruptor given her proven Soft-ground form.

Wee Dresser — the 58-day absence is the longest in the field; on soft ground after that layoff, watch her energy levels in the paddock and how she moves to post, as a below-par run on return cannot be ruled out and she may not fire first time back.

races.name: Caple - Built Into Every Great Kitchen Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Easterby who has been busy lately (ran just 3 days ago), and the soft going suits based on recent course form, but sim-going record reads 0 wins and 0 places from 5 efforts, making the ground less reliable a booster than it appears; headgear (p) noted.

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: [See above — already covered; Bellasio takes this slot instead]

runners_data.name: Spiritoftheblues
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent runner who has placed four times in five outings, all on good ground, meaning this is a soft-ground query though the yard has strong recent form; handles the mile well and could outrun odds if the going is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Albemagic
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with limited recent form (three runs, two placed) but soft-going experience in the most recent outing; likely to press Swift Salian from the off and the question is whether the stamina holds for a mile on this ground — likely a contested leader who helps set up others.

runners_data.name: Rewired
runners_data.note: Lengthy layoff of 472 days is the dominant concern here, and his form is entirely over extreme distances (16-17f) making this 1m trip a sharp drop that is hard to explain tactically; the soft going suits historically but the hold-up style and absence render him high-risk.

runners_data.name: Swift Salian
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a string of placed efforts at this trip on soft ground, though the form line shows an 8th last time out; will make the running and set whatever tempo emerges — if he stays honest rather than going flat-out, he retains a chance of lasting, but his 1W from 5 in similar going is workable.

runners_data.name: Arkenstaar
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has three wins and four places from seven soft-ground runs, making the going a genuine positive — raced 110 days ago but trainer Dods has a moderate 14-day strike rate; headgear worn (p) and if the pace is strong, this horse is worth watching from midfield.

runners_data.name: Zermatt Star
runners_data.note: Natural rear-of-field operator who is placed here in midfield because the race already holds too many hold-up runners to accommodate all at the back — the horse recorded a recent win on soft ground at this trip, but racing closer than ideal will compromise the signature late run; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type whose best recent efforts include a win and a second on soft ground, but like Zermatt Star it cannot occupy its natural rearward position given the crowd of closers in this field — the 7-day turnaround is fine and the going suits, but the positional compromise is real; STYLE_FIT of 0.91 noted.

runners_data.name: Bellasio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose last win came over 9f on good ground and who has run twice on soft-ish going recently without threatening; the 8-day turnaround is fine but soft ground form shows 5/15 with 1 win, suggesting the conditions are not strongly in his favour.

runners_data.name: Epidavros
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a b headgear flag and a going record of 0 wins and 3 places from 5 similar-ground runs — positioned in midfield rather than the rear because of redistribution, so the closing burst that defines this horse's best form is harder to engineer; modest OR of 64 limits ceiling.

races.paceDynamic: Swift Salian and Albemagic are the two confirmed front-runners here, and with both likely to press for the early lead on soft ground over a mile at Carlisle, this shapes as a genuinely contested gallop from the off — neither is a natural solo leader happy to dictate, meaning the pace is likely to be honest rather than brutal but consistent enough to stretch the field. The soft going (confirmed Good to Soft for the 4:47 slot, despite the race card listing soft) will amplify the stamina test and make it harder for hold-up horses to produce a telling late burst if the leaders have controlled the tempo from the front. The field holds more hold-up types than can be properly accommodated at the rear of the field — Zermatt Star, Epidavros, and Tee Aitch Aye are all genuine closers but are mapped to midfield because of the traffic of hold-up runners, meaning they are unlikely to get a true waiting ride and may race more prominently than ideal. This race shape most clearly favours prominent racers who can travel just behind the front two and pounce in the straight, with pace-on-pace likely to see the leaders tire on the soft ground and reward those racing handily without burning fuel early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Swift Salian and Albemagic set a honest-but-not-suicidal gallop and the race is run at a controlled tempo that suits handy types over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn off each other through the middle portion of the race, leaving prominent racers travelling just off the pace in the ideal position to accelerate into the straight on the testing ground; Hostility and Spiritoftheblues both possess the tactical speed and mile form to strike from this position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the early battle between Swift Salian and Albemagic is less fierce than expected and one settles into a controlled lead, preserving enough energy to hold on through soft ground.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner who gets an uncontested lead on soft going can sap the energy from chasers and hold on grimly as the ground dries their finish; Swift Salian's placed record in soft conditions and wide experience at this trip makes this viable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong and the front pair tie each other up badly, opening a gap for horses racing midfield to close strongly in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Soft ground combined with a fast-run mile can make the race run very long, giving runners with stamina reserves a late advantage; Arkenstaar's soft-ground wins and Tee Aitch Aye's recent soft-course form give them credentials here, though both are racing less naturally than ideal given redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart chaotically, the pace is extreme and every front-runner and prominent type flattens out, leaving genuine backmarkers to come from off the pace.
scenarios.body: This scenario is the least likely given that the redistributed hold-up types — Zermatt Star, Epidavros and Tee Aitch Aye — are unlikely to be in their true rearward positions, reducing the chance of a classic closer's swoop; Zermatt Star's win at this trip and trip on soft is the one viable late-run angle.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Swift Salian and Albemagic genuinely battle for the lead from the gates — if both commit fully to front-running, the pace will be strong enough on soft ground to blow the field apart and hand the race to prominent types like Hostility.

Rewired's 472-day absence and complete trip incompatibility (all career form at 16-17f) make him an unknown quantity and potential pacemaker disruptor if he is ridden aggressively to find a rhythm early.

Zermatt Star, Tee Aitch Aye and Epidavros are all natural closers crowded into midfield positions — if they race even closer than mapped, they will exhaust themselves and inflate the odds of a prominent-runner winner; monitor market moves to gauge which handler has accepted the positional compromise.

The going is confirmed Good to Soft for the 4:47 race slot despite the race card listing Soft — the ground is less demanding than the card implies, which slightly reduces the stamina advantage for proven soft-ground specialists and marginally improves the chance of front-runners lasting.

Tee Aitch Aye's jockey Jack Nicholls claims 3lb, reducing the horse's effective weight burden and potentially making it more competitive in a field where several rivals are carrying 130-140lbs on testing ground.

races.name: Logic's 40th Anniversary Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: One Night Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with soft-ground form (placed at 5/15 on similar going) and a recent 11-day turnaround under Sam James; needs the pace to truly collapse to get a clear run from the back, which is possible but not guaranteed here.

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has won three of his last five at 7f and boasts a soft-going win in that form string — 65 days off is worth monitoring but Jack Nicholls (3) taking the ride for Jardine (4/31 T14) is an eye-catching booking at this trip.

runners_data.name: Leopards Rock
runners_data.note: Three-year-old front-runner for Bethell who has not yet encountered genuinely soft ground; Connor Beasley takes over and will press on from the gate, but his stamina for a grinding 7f in this going is unproven and the dual-pace scenario could expose that.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: Tudhope-ridden prominent type for O'Meara with strong recent placed form at 7f and 8f on good ground; no soft-going form on record is a flag, though the step to better ground is not extreme and he arrives on the back of a 32-day break in good shape.

runners_data.name: Monsieur Kodi
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field at OR 75 and wears a hood; Fahey-trained seven-year-old with soft-ground place form but his last three runs have been over 6f on Tapeta — the return to turf at 7f on soft is the key question.

runners_data.name: They All Know Me
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won at 7f on Soft and has soft-ground placed form — the Fahey yard is firing (8/61 T14) and David Nolan rides; needs to improve on a recent OR-74 run, but a strong pace suits his style if he can find a clear passage.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Front-runner with blinkers and a hood fitted, returning after just 16 days; Davidson has placed 4/12 runners in the past fortnight and the horse won at 9f recently, but his soft-going record (0W1P from 3 runs) is modest and he faces a direct rival for the lead in Leopards Rock.

runners_data.name: Albeseeingyer
runners_data.note: Hollinshead's seven-year-old arrives with a run of 7f placed form on good ground and has genuine pace — but with the map crowded upfront, he is unlikely to secure his preferred prominent pitch and races out of role here, which tempers his chance considerably.

runners_data.name: Von Trotter
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent type who has won and been placed at 7f on good ground for Easterby; no soft-going experience on record is a concern on today's surface, but Billy Garritty rides and he arrives with a reliable each-way profile if conditions are not too testing.

runners_data.name: Circle Of Trust
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old who won at 7f on Soft and was placed again at 7f on Soft — blinkers fitted and Tom Eaves up; soft-ground credentials are the best in the field among the closers, and a truly-run pace would play to his strengths if he gets daylight.

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, returning quickly after just 5 days; blinkers on and placed at 7f on heavy, but shifted toward midfield on the map due to field congestion at the rear — his true closer's role may not fully materialise, softening his prospects in a pace-dependent scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Leopards Rock and Runninsonofagun are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 7f on Good To Soft ground at Carlisle, creating a genuinely honest and competitive early gallop rather than a slowly-run affair. Runninsonofagun wears a hood and has shown willingness to force the pace, while Leopards Rock is a young three-year-old who has raced prominently throughout — neither is likely to concede to the other cheaply. This contested lead on softening ground will stretch the field through the first half and set up a searching test of stamina in the closing stages, favouring horses who can travel economically in midfield or just off the pace before delivering a sustained late effort. The field contains more genuinely prominent-type runners than can comfortably occupy that ground — Albeseeingyer and Only Dream Big, both redistributed from their natural positions, are unlikely to secure the berths their style would normally demand, with Sandy Craic, The Gay Blade, and Monsieur Kodi better placed to hold prominent ground. The tactical verdict is clear: a contested pace on soft ground over 7f strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with stamina and soft-ground form, not leaders or those forced wide and backward.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Grinds Them Out
scenarios.trigger: If Leopards Rock and Runninsonofagun force an honest gallop that gradually depletes those racing prominently, setting up a grinding soft-ground finish.
scenarios.body: The sustained early pace burns off the front two inside the final two furlongs, leaving those travelling just off the pace with a decisive advantage as the ground bites; horses with proven soft-ground stamina and prominent-but-covered positions benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Clear Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Leopards Rock — finds a second wind and the runner-up settles just off them, turning it into a two-horse battle.
scenarios.body: A more controlled early pace than feared allows Leopards Rock to dictate at a manageable tempo and simply stretch clear from 2f out with Sandy Craic or The Gay Blade tracking close enough to pounce; the soft ground rewards a strong-traveller over the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners truly burn each other out in a fierce early duel and the pace collapses turning in, opening the race wide for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Circle Of Trust and One Night Thunder, both proven in soft conditions at 7f, would find themselves with a wall of beaten horses to pass but enough momentum if the race truly falls apart; Circle Of Trust's Soft-ground win and the front-runners' mutual destruction make this plausible but reliant on things going wrong up front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Runninsonofagun, blinkers on and freshened after 16 days, bowls along and the field fails to organise a coherent pursuit.
scenarios.body: Runninsonofagun's hood and recent form suggest he could dictate if Leopards Rock drops away early, leaving him to steal a lead that proves unassailable on the soft surface; this scenario demands that no prominent horse tracks efficiently, which is unlikely given the quality of Sandy Craic and The Gay Blade.

watchPoints.text: Leopards Rock and Runninsonofagun will compete for the lead from the off — watch whether either capitulates before halfway, as whichever controls the tempo first gains a material advantage.
Sandy Craic has no recorded soft-going form; if the ground rides more testing than Good To Soft in the afternoon, his prominent position could become a liability rather than an asset.

Albeseeingyer is unlikely to secure his natural prominent berth given the traffic ahead of him — watch whether Clifford Lee elects to drop him in or fights for position, as either choice carries risk.

Circle Of Trust is the most credentialled soft-ground hold-up horse in the field (two wins/places on Soft at 7f) — if the front two do burn each other out visibly by halfway, he is the one to track from the rear.

The Gay Blade's 65-day absence is worth monitoring in the betting market — if well-supported despite the layoff, it suggests Jardine has the horse ready and his soft-going win form makes him a serious player.
